newsitem.title: USA: Fisher Scientific CEO under fire - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Fisher Scientific CEO under fire - WSJ.

text.p: Fisher Scientific International Inc's largest shareholder, disappointed with the company's profit and stock performance, is moving to try to oust Chief Executive Paul Montrone, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Monday's electronic edition, the Journal said the shareholder, an investment partnership of the Bass brothers of Texas, has been talking with other large holders recently to seek support for the outster and other plans.
The partnership, Trinity I Fund LP, has suggested it is prepared to launch a takeover bid of up to $1 billion for Fisher if the company doesn't move to boost its share price.
Aside from possibly seeking Montrone's removal, the partnership's plans include a reversal of Fisher's acquisition strategy and a warehouse consolidation to cut costs and improve profit margins.
The partnership believes that Montrone, who is chairman of another company and has a consulting contract, is not devoting full attention to Fisher.
Montrone also is non-executive chairman of General Chemical Group Inc, a soda ash producer that, like Fisher, is based in Hampton, N.H.
Montrone and Fisher Chief Financial Officer Paul Meister also have formed Latona Associates Inc, which provides "strategic guidance and advice" to General Chemical.

A spokesman for Fisher said Montrone has held top jobs at as many as four publicly held companies in the past decade as part of the process of spinning out units of Henley Group, a diversified firm that once owned both Fisher and General Chemical.
Montrone, in an interview with the Journal, defended his business plan and said, "I think the company is going at full speed. ... The moves we're making are designed to enhance our multiple."
